The main takeaway from our work is that
the rights of Aboriginal peoples have been contested in the courts and the public sphere, and the way forward is to engage with the other as a subject, rather than as an object.
Indigenous peoples have been excluded from the rights discourse, and the way to include them is to reconfigure the way rights are understood and claimed, and the way they are exercised.
the I-Thou approach offers a model for the resolution of the Indigenous and non- Indigenous rights dilemma.
